spans.text: ...In the suburbs of Warsaw.
Rosita is asleep, her little head leaning against Pavel's leg.
Pavel is at a loss for what to do next. He stays put, not daring to move.
She is severely malnourished, both light and skinny, and it feels as though she might disappear into the wind if he just moved her a little.
What are these marks?
The other humans don't have these...
As he looks at the strange marks on Rosita's arms, a feeling of unease fills Pavel.
He opens his simple search engine and starts searching up the characteristics of those marks.
Several seconds later, he gets an answer.
ELID. Eurosky Low-Emission Infectious Disease.
Pavel remembers what his human supervisors said while working on the Siberian wastes.
...I'm not going in there, only you tin cans can survive down there. Humans who go out there would become ELIDs in minutes!
At that point you wouldn't even be let aboard the train, to say nothing of getting home!
It would seem it is a very infectious and very dangerous disease for humans.
Pavel's heart aches as she looks down at Rosita, who is sound asleep.He looks at her like he was looking at a pitiful rose that has been removed from its case and gnawed by maggots.
He wants to do something for Rosita.
After all, she is the first human he has seen after so long that made him feel that roses might exist.
"The Galatea Corporation has just released a new anti-ELID wonder drug—Idunn, which is both cheap and effective... "
"The drug labs under Galatea have been shut down..."
As piece after piece of ELID-related news streams past his eyes, his heart rises and falls like a rollercoaster.
If I could go to Berlin, then I might be able to find a cure...
How do humans heal their damaged bodies? Do they have some kind of human-specific machine oil?
Is this Idunn their hope for treatment?
Pavel notes down his thoughts in his neural cloud and decides to take Rosita to Berlin for treatment, and then to Bremen to find Berle Orphanage.
Pavel...
I had a dream where I went home...
Yeah, I'll send you home.
Rosita rubs her sleepy eyes and slowly sits up.
First we'll go to Berlin, and then to Bremen...
But I don't have any money...
It's alright. I have some money that I saved up.
Pavel looks down at the little bag that 634 has gave him. It's full of little rocks.
While he was on the intercontinental train, he learned that it was called Sardis Gold, or the raw form of gold bullion, a form of currency in human society.
Pavel doesn't know if it'll be enough to get Rosita back to Bremen, but he wants to try.
I met a scalper on the train. I'll ask her how to buy tickets.
Yup! I'll listen to you!
...Several hours later, Pavel returns to the abandoned house he found.
Upon hearing his footsteps, Rosita waves weakly at him.
You're back.
...What's wrong?
Pavel drags a massive suitcase over but doesn't speak.
How could he tell Rosita that she can't board the train because she is sick, that she can only sneak aboard in a suitcase?
Pavel looks at her blank eyes and in the end, he decides to lie to her.
I'm sorry, Rosita. I only had enough money for one ticket, so I'm afraid you'll have to suffer a little...
It's alright. I'm happy just to be heading home!
...Okay. Let's see if it fits.
Pavel opens the suitcase and lays it on the ground, then gently lays Rosita inside.
After Pavel closes the suitcase, he hears Rosita giggling inside.
What?
I remembered my time in the orphanage. I'd always hide in places like this, until she found me...
Pavel, tell me a story.
I often hear you flipping pages, so tell me about the books you've read.
Alright.
Pavel sits beside the suitcase and Rosita curls up quietly inside.
Once upon a time, there was a prince that came from an asteroid. His asteroid was small—much, much smaller than our Earth.
He was the only person on his asteroid. He lived there with his rose.
Rose?
Oh yes. The rose was a strange one, fragile and sensitive, and she could only survive inside a glass case.
In order to protect herself, the rose sprouted thorns all over herself, but always pricked the Prince, who was closest to her.
The Prince could not bear it and decided to leave that asteroid and go see the world.
I... don't think the rose did it on purpose.
Yeah, I agree.
After leaving his asteroid and having many adventures, the prince realized that the fragile rose had simply wanted to embrace him.
But because of the thorns that she had grown to survive, she couldn't keep herself from hurting him.
Did the prince go back and make up with the rose?
Later on, every time the prince looked up at the starry sky, he saw each and every star as that rose—
His unique, irreplaceable rose.
Rosita's eyes close again, and Pavel pulls a blanket over her.
Someone once told me that this world was no longer suitable for fragile roses to live in.
But then I found you, so young and small that you hadn't even been able to grow thorns to protect yourself.
I want to see you grow proud and strong without having to sprout thorns, so you can embrace your loved ones without harming them.
When that time comes, I will report to the recycling station, and when I do, I'm sure the sky will be filled with roses...
Pavel looks at Rosita's sleeping face and imagines the night sky with roses blooming across it.
...Several days later, aboard the "Future", in the second-class carriage.
Boom—
A massive impact flings the suitcase from the baggage rack and throws Rosita out.
ROSITA!
Pavel...
The cabin spins end over end, but Pavel's gaze is firmly fixed on Rosita.
She's fallen from her glass case again, rolling around in this dangerous world...
Once the carriage comes to rest, Pavel rushes to her side.
Pavel... I'm fine...
Good lord! Look! There's an infected here!!!
No wonder the purification system kept going off all this time... We need to get her off the train!
Don't touch her!
Whoosh—
Pavel swings his wrench, an inexplicable courage burning in his heart.
Is he insane?!
I won't let any of you hurt her!
Pavel, who has always been docile, suddenly snarls at the humans and Dolls around him. The wrench in his hand is no longer just a simple track maintenance tool, but a dragon-slaying sword...
"But in herself alone she is more important than all the hundreds of you other roses—"
"And now here is my secret, a very simple secret—it is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye."
Behind him is his eternal angel, his rose for which there is no substitute...
He must fight on, for Rosita's sake.
